newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Higher EU wheat output seen in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Higher EU wheat output seen in 1997.

text.p: European Union wheat production is expected to increase further in 1997 following a halving of set-aside to five percent and excellent planting conditions for winter-sown crops, trade sources said.
"The harvest will be at least as good as this year," said a trade source, adding, "Even if yields are only normal the area will be larger."
EU soft wheat production totalled 91 million tonnes in 1996, up 13.6 percent from last year, Coceral, the EU grain trade lobby said on December 3.
Increased output followed a 3.1 percent increase in the wheat area to 13.8 million hectares and a rise in average yields to 6.59 tonnes per hectare from 5.98 tonnes in 1995.
Coceral may have preliminary estimates in February of sowings for the 1997 harvest.

French, German and British farmers, taking advantage of firm EU prices, have expanded winter wheat plantings, especially of high yield feed varieties. Good moisture content has helped crop development.
But farmers in some other northern countries, such as Denmark, have switched to malting barley, the source added.
In Spain, ravaged by drought in recent years, heavy rain in the southern region of Andalusia has damaged wheat and other crops.
Other southern EU countries are also reported to have had more than adequate rainfall.
